active.title: [bug] Pi provider plugins skip custom auth.apiKey.login

new.body:
Adding a second face of the same `methods()` decision, from a real package rather than a fixture.

**Case:** a pi provider registers `auth.apiKey` with **no custom `login`** — its credential comes from local state (a browser session cookie sealed with DPAPI), so there is no key a user could type. `magpie` still offers `{ type: "api", label: "API key" }`, and login cannot proceed.

**What pi does with an `apiKey` auth that has no login.** `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` fabricates one — `dist/core/provider-composer.js`:

```js
// OAuth-only providers get no fabricated API-key login method.
if (!inherited && rawKey === undefined && oauth) return undefined
...
login: inherited?.login ?? (async (interaction) => ({
  type: "api_key",
  key: await interaction.prompt({ type: "secret", message: "Enter API key" }),
})),
```

So "no `login` in the package" does not mean "pi needs no key input": pi substitutes an "Enter API key" prompt. OAuth-only is the one shape that skips it. That also marks the edge of the fix described above — *"A provider that wrote no login keeps magpie's key field"* means a local-credential provider that wrote no login is still asked for a key it does not have.

**Real package:** `dsh-connect-doubao`, with a pi entry added in my fork: https://github.com/takomitkm/dsh-connect-doubao/tree/feat/pi-package. Doubao's credential is a QR sign-in session cookie, read per request by a loopback shim; no key exists. Declared as `apiKey`, magpie asked for one.

**Workaround that works today:** declare the provider OAuth-only (`auth: { oauth: { login() { …QR sign-in… }, refresh(), toAuth() } }`). Then `pi.js`'s `methods()` yields exactly one `oauth` method and pi fabricates no key login. Checked against magpie 0.1.4611: replaying `methods()` over the built entry gives `[{ type: "oauth", label: "浏览器扫码登录豆包" }]`, and `magpie plugin list` shows the provider with its models.

**Question:** could `pi.js` mirror `host.js`'s keyless handling for this case — a package's own `apiKey` auth whose `resolve()` answers from ambient or local state, offered as one `keyless` `api` method with no personal-key entry? The OpenCode side already documents this (`keyless: true`, "Fixed-credential sign-in" in `docs/subsystems/provider-plugins.md`); the pi side has no equivalent (`keyless` does not appear in `pi.js`). A line in that doc saying pi providers need OAuth-only or a custom login to avoid the key prompt would also save the next person this round trip.

issue.title: gateway: deepseek-flash 在 DeepSeek 的 Responses API 上不执行 web_search（静默忽略），但 magpie 按 host 当它会自己搜；它在 Anthropic API 上会搜

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 现象

在 Codex（0.171.0，`web_search = "live"`）里用 `deepseek/deepseek-flash`。Settings › Web search 的 "searchAll"（有自带搜索的模型也由 magpie 代搜）**关闭**时，模型拿不到任何搜索能力：它直接作答，或者说自己没有搜索工具。HTTP 200，不报错，Routing 里也看不出问题。把 searchAll **打开**后搜索就正常了。

magpie 0.1.4650（源码在 a53f08e11 核对）。

## 原因

magpie 按 host 判断"provider 自己会搜"（`internal/gateway/search.go` 的 `searchHosts`）。`api.deepseek.com` 在 Responses 和 Anthropic 两栏里都有，所以 DeepSeek 的**所有模型**在这两个接口上都被当成会自己搜。searchAll 关闭时，Codex 的 hosted `{"type":"web_search","external_web_access":true}` 会被原样转给 DeepSeek 的 `/v1/responses`，但 deepseek-flash 在那里会**静默忽略**这个工具。

DeepSeek 文档写明了这一点（https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/responses_api ）：`tools` 一行写的是 "`web_search` supported with `deepseek-v4-pro`; other types ignored"，`response.web_search_call.*` 事件标注为 "`deepseek-v4-pro` only"。

## 核对过程

**1. Codex 发出的请求。** 用临时 `CODEX_HOME` 让 Codex 0.171.0 把请求发到本地抓包服务。`/backend-api/codex/responses` 的 tools 里有 `{"type":"web_search","external_web_access":true}`，客户端这边正常。

**2. magpie 转发出去的请求。** 用 gateway 包现有的测试工具（`searchSandbox`、`searchesOn`）搭了一个假的 DeepSeek，把抓到的 Codex 请求原样重放：

| searchAll | 入口 | DeepSeek 收到的请求 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 关 | `/backend-api/codex/responses`、`/v1/responses` | `/v1/responses`，带原生 `web_search` |
| 开 | 同上 | `/v1/responses`，带 magpie 的 `web_search` function |

magpie 的转发和它的判断是一致的，问题出在判断本身。

**3. 真实 DeepSeek API，同一条提问**（"Use web search: latest Go release? cite URL"）：

| 模型 | Responses `/v1/responses` + `web_search` | Anthropic `/anthropic/v1/messages` + `web_search_20250305` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | **会搜**：1 次中 1 次，输出含 2 个 `web_search_call` | **会搜**：2 次中 2 次，`web_search_requests` 为 2–3 |
| `deepseek-flash` | **不搜**：4 次中 0 次，输出只有 `reasoning` + `message`；加 `"tool_choice":"required"` 也一样（2 次） | **会搜**：2 次中 2 次，`web_search_requests` 为 3–4 |

复现：

```sh
for M in deepseek-v4-pro deepseek-flash; do printf "%s: " $M
curl -s https://api.deepseek.com/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"stream\":false,\"tools\":[{\"type\":\"web_search\",\"external_web_access\":true}],\"input\":\"Use web search: latest Go release? cite URL\"}" \
  | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print([o.get('type') for o in d.get('output',[])])"; done

for M in deepseek-v4-pro deepseek-flash; do printf "%s: " $M
curl -s https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1/messages -H "x-api-key: $DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"max_tokens\":2000,\"tools\":[{\"type\":\"web_search_20250305\",\"name\":\"web_search\",\"max_uses\":3}],\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Use web search: latest Go release? cite URL\"}]}" \
  | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print([b.get('type') for b in d.get('content',[])], d.get('usage',{}).get('server_tool_use'))"; done
```

## 修复时要注意：flash 在 Anthropic 上是会搜的

#2729 和它下面的修复分支（fork 上的 `fix/2729-gateway-deepseek-s-search-api`，a8de723e5）把"flash 在 Anthropic 端点上会不会搜"留作未知。上面的实测说明它**会搜**，这对修法有影响。

如果只把 Responses 改成按模型判断（flash 不搜），flash 在 Anthropic 上仍然算会搜。对 Responses 客户端带 `web_search` 的请求，`internal/gateway/gateway.go` 的 handle 里那段 `for _, t := range s.usable(p, model) { if searchesFor(p, t, model, request) && !magpieSearches(...) { ... to = t } }` 会把请求挪到 Anthropic。Codex **每一轮**都带 `web_search`，所以 Codex 用 deepseek-flash 的每一轮都会被翻译成 Anthropic 再发给 DeepSeek，推理内容回传、缓存命中这些都可能因此变化。上面那个分支的测试只覆盖了 Responses，碰不到这一点（它的 fake 只看 `/v1/responses`）。

两种可选的方向：

1. **flash 在 Responses 上由 magpie 代搜，请求不换协议**：效果和打开 searchAll 一样，只对 flash 生效。需要在上面那段循环里，不为搜索把 deepseek-flash 的 Responses 请求挪到 Anthropic。
2. **挪到 Anthropic，用 DeepSeek 自己的搜索**：只改按模型的判断，接受 Codex + flash 每一轮都换协议。

不管选哪种，下面这些都不受影响：deepseek-v4-pro 在 Responses 上的原生搜索；Anthropic 客户端（Claude Code 等）用 flash 时的原生搜索；DeepSeek 当 searcher 时走 Anthropic 的原生搜索（`searchBody` 是 Messages 请求）。

## 目前的绕过办法

- 用 deepseek-flash：打开 searchAll。
- 想用 DeepSeek 自己的搜索：Codex 换用 `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`，可以关闭 searchAll。

## 关联

- #2729：同一个问题，open。本 issue 补上 flash 在两个接口上的实测，以及 Anthropic 端会搜带来的协议挪动问题。
- #512：把 `api.deepseek.com` 加进 `searchHosts[Responses]` 的来源。当时用 deepseek-flash 只确认了 DeepSeek 在回显里接受了这个工具，没有确认它真的执行了搜索。

active.title: gateway: server-managed tools (web_search/web_fetch) silently dropped on translated routes — 200 OK, no error or capability signal

new.body:
This still happens on v0.1.4726 (`1ee1a87b`), on a route the summary doesn't list. The client sends an OpenAI Responses request carrying `{"type":"web_search"}`, and it goes to a provider plugin that does not search by itself.

- `searchesFor` is false, so the flag is cleared before the upstream request is built (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:8840-8843`).
- With no searcher available, `canSearchFor(p)` is false as well, so magpie does not answer the search itself (`gateway.go:10027`).
- The client gets a plain 200 with no search call. Nothing in the headers, the usage or the stream marks that the tool was removed.

From in front of the gateway, three cases look the same: the model chose not to search, the search found nothing, and the tool was taken away. The last one happens, for example, when the searcher's sign-in is missing after a container restart. The `X-Magpie-Tools-Dropped` header in the branch above is the signal we would read to notice it.

active.title: Pi 集成：Google 模型未配置为 google-generative-ai，仍继承 openai-completions

new.body:
看了当前 `main` 的协议转换实现，以及 Pi SDK 的更新，有几个问题值得重新评估：

**1. Pi SDK 已支持自定义 fetch**

Pi [v1.6.0](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/ai/CHANGELOG.md) 已为 `google-generative-ai` 添加自定义 `fetch` 支持（[#12103](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12103)）。

因此原先的限制对新版 Pi 已不成立。不过 Raft 仍使用旧版 SDK，且与 Pi 共享 `models.json`，不能直接恢复原生协议而忽略 Raft 的兼容性。

**2. Chat → Gemini 转换仍存在信息丢失**

- **文本 `thoughtSignature` 丢失**：[`codeAssistDecoder`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/gateway/codeassist.go) 会产生 `KTextSig`，但 [`chatEncoder.event()`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/gateway/chat.go#L1746-L1790) 没有处理它。工具调用签名虽然通过 `signedID()` 保留，但普通文本 Part 的签名无法往返。
- **Thinking 状态不完整**：Chat 路径只能传递可见思考文本，不能完整保留 Gemini 原生 Thinking Part 及其签名关联。这个问题也值得检查原生 Gemini 路径经过 IR 重建时的行为。
- **`xhigh` 降级**：[`thinkingConfig()`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/main/internal/gateway/codeassist.go#L1006-L1069) 对普通 Chat 请求的 `xhigh` 通常映射为 `high`，即使上游模型实际支持 `xhigh`。

前两项可能影响多轮推理状态的连续性，第三项会影响实际思考强度。

**建议：**

- 重新评估 Pi 恢复 `google-generative-ai` 的可行性，同时为仍使用旧 SDK 的 Raft 寻找独立兼容方案。
- 如果继续使用 Chat 转换，补充文本签名往返、Thinking Part 和思考等级的测试，明确哪些信息可以无损保留、哪些必须降级。
- 不需要为了 #3282 实现通用跨协议 Opaque Envelope；这里只需处理 Gemini ↔ Chat 的具体兼容问题。

以上是基于当前源码的检查，尚未通过真实 Google AI Studio 账号进行端到端复现。

原因：Kimi Code 用它自己的登录直连时，会话文件里的模型名是它配置里的键 `kimi-code/k3-256k`。magpie 把这类本地会话记在“未知提供商”下，按这个全名去找官方价格，找不到，于是你在 Kimi Code（China）里设的价格从没被用上。

现在这类调用按你在 Providers 里添加的 Kimi Code 会员来计价，顺序如下：
1. 你为这个模型设的价格，前缀所指的那一个会员优先；
2. 该会员的默认价格，即对应的 Kimi API 模型价格，并按它的时段倍率计算；
3. 一个会员都没添加时，按 Kimi API 的公开价格；
4. kimi-for-coding（K2.8 Preview）不在 API 上，仍不计价。

Usage、Requests 和 Sessions 页都按这个规则计价，以前的记录也会重新算出费用。

issue.title: Routing group: Claude Code auto-compaction mid-turn drops the turn's rule and use-effort (waits: true for the rest of the turn)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### magpie version

0.1.4623 (latest; also 0.1.4582)

### Where

Gateway only

### OS

macOS 27 (arm64)

### Agent, provider and model

Claude Code 2.1.330 (also 2.1.329) → local magpie gateway → an auto routing group (`routing: order`, `stays: auto`) with an intent classifier, a `compact` rule and intent rules that set `use-effort`.

### Steps to reproduce

**Summary.** When Claude Code auto-compacts in the middle of a user turn, the turn's rule is lost. Every normal request that follows in the same turn routes with `rule: {n: 0, waits: true, turn: 1}` and no `useEffort`, so the group's default member order and the agent's own effort are used. `magpie group rule help` says of `compact`: *"it is not the turn's model, and the requests after it go on as before"*. This reproduces in a fresh session with no rule edits.

The group I used has these rules:

```
1 compacting → group/deepseek-v4.1-flash, codex/gpt-6.2-sol at low
…
9 intent "an easy task: a quick question, a small edit, a lookup, or running a command" → opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash at low
```

Its first member is a group whose first model is Opus 5.5. Any rule whose model is not the group's first member, and whose `use-effort` differs from the agent's, shows the problem most clearly.

1. Make a chain of synthetic files. Each file ends with the name of the next one, so a single turn makes several tool calls and still has work left when compaction fires:

   ```bash
   WORK=$(mktemp -d); cd "$WORK"
   python3 -I - <<'PY'
   import random
   from pathlib import Path
   words = """amber basin cedar delta ember fjord grove harbor island jasper kettle lagoon meadow nectar orchard
   pebble quarry ridge summit thicket upland valley willow yarrow zephyr anchor bramble canyon dune estuary
   falcon glacier heron inlet juniper kestrel lantern marsh nettle osprey prairie quill reed sparrow tundra""".split()
   rng = random.Random(29811)
   names = ['start.txt'] + [f'part{i}.txt' for i in range(1, 8)]
   for i, name in enumerate(names):
       with Path(name).open('x') as f:
           for _ in range(380):
               print(' '.join(rng.choice(words) for _ in range(12)), file=f)
           print('NEXT:', names[i+1] if i+1 < len(names) else 'END', file=f)
   PY
   SID=$(uuidgen | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z'); echo "$SID"
   ```

2. In a second terminal, follow the session's routes. A route id can appear several times as its state changes, so dedupe by `id`:

   ```bash
   SID=<the uuid>; seq=0
   while :; do
     event=$(curl -fsS --max-time 35 "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/magpie/route?session=$SID&after=$seq&wait=25") || break
     next=$(jq -r '.seq // 0' <<< "$event")
     if [ "$next" != "$seq" ]; then
       jq -c '.route | select(. != null) | {id,kind,asked_effort,effort,rule:(.rule|{n,held,waits,turn,useEffort,tokens}),first_try:.tries[0].model}' <<< "$event"
       seq=$next
     fi
   done
   ```

3. Run one turn. `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` only makes compaction come sooner. Long real tasks hit the same thing at the default threshold.

   ```bash
   ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3425 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$MAGPIE_KEY" \
   CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=20 claude --bare -p \
     "Start by reading start.txt in this folder with the Read tool. The last line of each file names the next file to read, so read each file in full; keep following the chain one file at a time until a file's last line says END. Then reply with the file names in the order you read them." \
     --model group/smart-split --tools Read --allowedTools Read --strict-mcp-config \
     --output-format stream-json --verbose --session-id "$SID"
   ```

4. Control: run it again with a new UUID and `DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1` in place of the override.

### What happened, and what you expected

`C` is a `kind: compact` request (rule 1). `W` is a normal request with `rule.n: 0, waits: true`.

- **Auto-compaction (0.1.4582 and 0.1.4623, same result):** `9 9 9 9 C W W C 9 9 9`
- **No compaction (control):** `9` × 9

| Request | rule | asked → sent effort | first try |
|---|---|---|---|
| last request before compaction | `n: 9, turn: 1, useEffort: low` | high → low | GLM-5.3-Flash |
| auto-compaction | `n: 1, useEffort: low` | high → low | DeepSeek Flash |
| first request after it | `n: 0, waits: true, turn: 1`, no `useEffort` | high → **high** | **Opus 5.5** |

Claude Code reported the first compaction with `preserved_segment` (35,252 → 10,021 tokens). After the second compaction, which had no preserved segment (43,580 → 2,157 tokens), the next request was classified again and matched rule 9. No new user message was sent. That is a reclassification, not the turn's rule being kept.

The same fixture with different prompts loses rule 7 (`codex/gpt-6.2-sol, group/mid at medium`: Sonnet/medium → Sol/high, `7 7 7 C W W W C W W W`) and rule 8 (`group/mid at medium`: `8×5 C W×3 C W`).

In three long real coding runs (each phase one `claude -p` turn, later phases `--resume` with a new user message), all six phases that compacted showed `W` right after their first compaction, and it stayed for the rest of the phase. That is 462 requests that lost rule 6's `xhigh` and went out at the agent's `high`. One example: `6 C W×22 C W×25 C W×19 C W×16 C W×75 C W×40`. Phases without compaction kept their rule throughout (`7×36`, `7×38`, `7×53`).

These cases did **not** produce `W`:
- auto-compaction just before the first request of a new user turn (`C 9 9`)
- a standalone `/compact` between turns, followed by a new message (`9 9`)
- the next real user message after a `W` phase, which is classified again

**Expected.** The compaction request may go to its own cheap model. After it, the rest of the same turn, including tool-result continuations, should keep the turn's rule: its model order and its `use-effort`, until the next real user message. If magpie can't match the turn reliably, falling back to classifying the original user message would be better than `waits`. The compaction summary itself should not be treated as a user message.

**Likely cause (from source at v0.1.4623).**
- [`ruleKey` / `firstWords`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.4623/internal/gateway/rules.go#L148-L185) key the turn's decision on group + session + a hash of the first user text.
- [`turnIn`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.4623/internal/gateway/affinity.go#L404-L460) recounts turns from the request's messages.
- The [compact branch of `ruleFor`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.4623/internal/gateway/rules.go#L249-L279) only picks a model for the summary and does not carry the turn's state over.
- For a within-turn request whose key is missing or whose stored turn number differs, [`ruleFor` sets `Waits`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.4623/internal/gateway/rules.go#L280-L315).

A compacted transcript changes the first user text and the turn count, so either check can fail. I did not capture the request bodies or keys, so I can't say which one fired for each request. The rule-handling code (`rules.go`, `compacting.go`, `turnIn`) is identical in [v0.1.4582…v0.1.4623](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/v0.1.4582...v0.1.4623).

Related: #3434, the same key structure on Codex compaction, where the symptom was reclassification rather than `waits`. Any fix should keep subagents that share the session id in turns of their own.

### Error text or logs

No errors: every request returned 200. The evidence is the `GET /v1/magpie/route` states shown above.

issue.title: [Bug] Codex Session routing groups share fallback affinity across threads and lose it after compaction

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### magpie version

The original affinity regression was reproduced on v0.1.4627 and on main at `a53f08e`. The expanded regression also fails on the first fix at `0a3d13a` and passes at `90c6a99`.

### Where

Gateway only

### OS

Windows amd64, build 26200

### Agent, provider and model

Codex Responses requests to an In order routing group with **Stays: Session**. The regression uses two loopback providers with distinct models and a matching High effort rule that prefers one of them.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Send a High effort root-thread request with a session ID, thread ID and native turn ID. Make the rule's preferred provider return HTTP 503 so the backup answers.
2. Restore the preferred provider and clear its rest. Replay the root's native turn with a replacement summary as the opening.
3. Start a child thread with the same session and opening but its own thread ID. Change the root's effort to Medium and test another outage on the member serving the root.

### What happened, and what you expected

The rule could move the root back to the recovered provider after a transcript replacement. A child could inherit the root's route, and a rate-limited account could hand a sealed child task to a second account.

The patch shares the session and thread identity between rule decisions and provider, account and model affinity. The recovered preference no longer displaces a healthy fallback when the rule and effort are unchanged. A new child still chooses its own route. An explicit effort change evaluates the rules again, and ordinary requests still fail over when their bound member fails.

The gateway reads Codex's `client_metadata` turn metadata first, then tries the `thread-id` header. A request without a usable thread uses the existing session or opening key. A sealed child task with a named parent can only reach the parent's recorded key or account, including when the child has no usable thread ID. A thread establishes a new binding on its first successful reply under the session-scoped key.

### Verification

```sh
go test ./internal/gateway -run '^TestCodexGroupSessionAffinity' -count=10
go test -race ./internal/gateway -run '^TestCodexGroupSessionAffinity' -count=3
```

The tests fail on the previous fix with the original gateway code restored. They reproduce the rule displacing a fallback, invalid metadata masking a valid header, a same-ID thread borrowing affinity from another session, and a sealed task reaching another account. The fixed branch passes both commands and the related gateway rule, effort, affinity, compaction and sealed-task tests. Windows and Linux (`nogui`) builds and `go vet` passed. The combined patch applies cleanly to official main at `b704e4f`.

The earlier Windows full-suite run found failures. A bounded rerun on both official main at `b704e4f` and the fix reproduced the same four failures: `TestFoldersJoinedOnce`, `TestImageFromLeavesTheRest`, `TestLivePathNamedOnce` and `TestAppliedOfParsesAnUnchangedFileOnce`. The compaction regression replays transcript replacement through the real handler using loopback providers. Live Codex compaction was not exercised.

### Restart follow-up

`90c6a99` restores the saved fallback after restart, but the in-memory rule decision is gone. If transcript replacement removes the text that matched the original rule, the gateway can pick a different rule and move the thread back to the recovered primary.

`928d344` saves the last successful Codex Session rule decision in the same `affinity.json` entry as the provider, account and model binding. The same native turn restores that decision when the rule configuration and requested effort still match. On a new turn, rule evaluation runs again and an unchanged matching rule can keep the healthy fallback. An effort change, a rule edit or an unavailable fallback can still change the route. Older entries without a saved rule decision remain readable.

```sh
go test ./internal/gateway -run '^TestCodexGroupSessionAffinityRuleSurvivesRestart$' -count=10
go test -race ./internal/gateway -run '^Test(CodexGroupSessionAffinity|AffinitySurvivesRestart|AffinityFileBounded|StickSurvivesDaysAway)' -count=3
```

The regression fails on `90c6a99`. It writes the affinity file, clears both in-memory caches and starts a new gateway with loopback providers. Both commands passed on the updated branch, along with the related gateway tests and Windows and Linux (`nogui`) builds and `go vet`. The combined patch applies to the checked official baseline `b704e4f`.

### Fix branch

Would a maintainer merge [`fix/codex-session-thread-affinity`](https://github.com/wizardpc-com/magpie/tree/fix/codex-session-thread-affinity), now at [`928d344`](https://github.com/wizardpc-com/magpie/commit/928d3444594308a43969f15986f8d6a1e1c12bc8)?

Related to #3434 for the compaction trigger. That issue tracks classifier re-evaluation. This report covers provider, account and model affinity.

issue.title: [Bug] Hide accounts masks routing-group references using model picker aliases

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### magpie version

`v0.1.3960` in the running app. The same behavior reproduces with the masking code from [`v0.1.4633`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/releases/tag/v0.1.4633) / [`2a2a8d73`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/commit/2a2a8d734210dd22785280513bad64036c2063d3) in an isolated browser fixture. I did not run the full newer build.

### Where

GUI (`magpie web`, Routing groups)

### OS

Android ARM64 (Termux), Chromium 141.

### Agent, provider and model

No agent request is needed. The affected group ID is `auto-claude-sonnet-4-5`, and its agent-facing reference is `auto/claude-sonnet-4-5`. The loaded model picker state contains an `options[]` entry whose `alias` is `claude-sonnet-4-5`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a catalog with an automatic group `auto/<model>` and a model picker option whose `alias` equals `<model>`.
2. Turn on **Hide accounts** and open **Routing groups**.
3. Compare the reference on the group card with **Agents pick it as** in the group's editor.

For a browser fixture, feed `noteAccounts()` a state shaped like `{"options":[{"value":"example-option","alias":"sample-routing-model"}]}`. Render `auto/sample-routing-model` in the card's `.mdl` element and after `Agents pick it as` in the editor's `.hint` element, then apply **Hide accounts**. No real account needs to be present for either reference to be masked.

### What happened, and what you expected

**TL;DR:** **Hide accounts** changes a valid routing reference into blurred stand-in letters in both the Groups list and the group editor. It should keep routing references readable without revealing account identities.

- **Observed:** Both places display `auto/troaieumttamottli`. The editor's actual `ID` input still reads `auto-claude-sonnet-4-5`, and the group's `ref` in `/api/groups` is still `auto/claude-sonnet-4-5`. This is a display issue, not a change to the stored group or returned reference.
- **Expected:** Both places display `auto/claude-sonnet-4-5` with **Hide accounts** on. Actual account identities and addresses should still be masked.
- **Source:** [`api()` forwards response data to the account collector](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/2a2a8d734210dd22785280513bad64036c2063d3/internal/gui/assets/app.js#L227). [`noteAccounts()` collects string `alias` values from objects not marked `named`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/2a2a8d734210dd22785280513bad64036c2063d3/internal/gui/assets/app.js#L24583), including `options[].alias` from `/api/state`. The [address-only label exceptions](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/2a2a8d734210dd22785280513bad64036c2063d3/internal/gui/assets/app.js#L24678) do not cover the [group card reference](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/2a2a8d734210dd22785280513bad64036c2063d3/internal/gui/assets/plugins/routing/client.js#L7533) or the [editor reference hint](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/2a2a8d734210dd22785280513bad64036c2063d3/internal/gui/assets/plugins/routing/client.js#L7852).
- **Related:** #3656 was fixed by [commit `9097687a3`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/commit/9097687a31ab0fd32a31c0b478099bb1ba1b535a), which is [already included in `v0.1.3960`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/9097687a31ab0fd32a31c0b478099bb1ba1b535a...v0.1.3960). Its protection for selected plan and model labels still works. The remaining gap is that a model picker alias is collected as an account name and the two routing-group fields are not protected. [#1973](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/1973) concerns project names in Sessions.

### Error text or logs

No request error. The affected DOM span is `.pii` with `filter: blur(2.2px)`. The isolated fixture masks both group references only after the model option enters the account collector; `.model-value` remains readable and a synthetic email is still masked.

**AI assistance:** AI helped trace the UI behavior, verify it with a synthetic fixture, and draft and submit this report.

active.title: plugins: `magpie plugin add`, a backup's restore and a sync replace a plugin of the same package without saying so

issue.title: A restore or sync brings a plugin's code but not its options, so a plugin-declared provider list stays as it was

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### What happens

A plugin's `options` are part of the providers part of a backup, but they are only applied to a plugin **that isn't installed yet**. When the plugin is already here, `provider.AddPlugins` skips it entirely (`internal/provider/backup.go`: `if e.Spec == "" || plugin.IsPath(e.Spec) || here[plugin.Name(e.Spec)] { continue }`), so `e.Options` and `e.Off` are never written. `davsync.bring` calls it and logs only failures, so nothing says the options were left behind — and `magpie webdav restore` still reports the providers part as restored.

For a plugin whose options decide **how many providers it registers**, "Restored from the server: providers" is then untrue: the plugin keeps registering the provider list of the old, empty options.

My case (`github:jingyi0605/magpie-newapi`): its `sites` option turns one pooled `newapi` provider into one provider per site. The other computer had three `sites`; this one had none, so it kept a single `newapi` with all three accounts (33 models) instead of the three providers. Providers, keys, sign-ins and plugin code had all arrived — only the option that shapes them hadn't.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On computer A: `magpie plugin add github:jingyi0605/magpie-newapi`, then give it options with two or more sites, e.g. `magpie plugin options github:jingyi0605/magpie-newapi '{"sites":[{"id":"relay-a","name":"Relay A"},{"id":"relay-b","name":"Relay B"}]}'`. Sign in one account. A shows two providers, `relay-a` and `relay-b`.
2. Sync A to WebDAV.
3. On computer B: install the same plugin with no options (`magpie plugin add github:jingyi0605/magpie-newapi`). B shows one provider, `newapi`.
4. On B: `magpie webdav on <address>` (or `magpie webdav restore` in follow mode), then `magpie webdav` and/or `magpie plugin options github:jingyi0605/magpie-newapi`.

### What I expected

B ends up with `relay-a` and `relay-b`, as A has them — at least from an explicit **Restore** (and while this computer follows the server, where the server's setup is the one to take). Where that can't be done automatically, the restore says which installed plugins were left as they are, so "Restored from the server: providers" doesn't claim a shape it didn't bring.

### What happened instead

B keeps one `newapi` provider. `magpie webdav` says `Restored from the server: providers, agents' models, library`, and `magpie plugin options github:jingyi0605/magpie-newapi` prints nothing. Nothing is logged or shown about the options.

Applying the options by hand with the exact array the backup holds fixes it at once (`magpie plugin options … '{"sites":[…]}'`): the three providers appear without reinstalling the plugin or touching the sign-ins, which is what makes me think the missing step is only this write.

### Cause, as far as I could read it in the source

- `internal/provider/backup.go`, `AddPlugins`: an installed plugin (matched by `plugin.Name(e.Spec)`) is skipped, so `plugin.SetOptions`/`plugin.SetOff` run only for the plugins it adds.
- `internal/davsync/davsync.go`, `bring(…, "providers")`: calls `addPlugins` and `log.Printf`s failed specs only, so a skip is silent.
- `internal/davsync/restore.go`, `Restore`: lists the parts it brought in (`Notice.Here`), not the plugins whose options it didn't apply.

So this is the same family as #3927 (a sync or restore changes what a plugin is without saying so), from the other side: here it changes nothing and says nothing, and the providers page then shows a provider list from before the sync.

I would not ask a two-way sync to overwrite a plugin's options blindly — those can carry this computer's own choices (the `sites` above may omit `url` on purpose, so each account supplies its address). A reasonable reading: apply them on Restore and while following the server, keeping the replaced options in the sync folder like other replaced parts; in a two-way sync, keep this computer's and name the plugin in the sync's notices.

### Version

magpie 0.1.4720 on Windows, syncing over WebDAV, follow-server mode, manual sync. Observed after `Restore` had already brought providers in. The `AddPlugins` skip is still there in v0.1.4722 (`internal/provider/backup.go`), so I believe it is still current, but I only ran the flow above on 0.1.4720.

issue.title: fix(usage): carry the soonest-expiring OfficeAce bucket on the longest window

repository.name: magpie-officeace
repository.description: OfficeAce (Huawei Cloud AgentArts / MaaS) provider plugin for magpie: 26 models, credit windows, token rates and daily check-in.

issue.body:
Fixes the OfficeAce half of yetone/magpie#4923.

## Why the plugin

magpie's Use before expiry takes the tighter pace of two budget windows (Opus's own week beside the general one), and `TestAllowancePace` pins that. OfficeAce reports the daily check-in bonus as a separate budget window: 50 points reset at the end of the day (the remaining hours count down 5→4→3), while 300 points reset in 30 days. The month's 0.139 therefore hid the day's 25, and Trae's 2,600 credits over ten days (0.405) led the route group.

The fix follows the maintainer's suggested path in #4923: the plugin carries the soonest lapse, as the CodeArts plugin already does for its total window. It does not change min→max in magpie.

## What changed

- The **longest-lived live window** gets `runsOutAt` / `runsOut` from the **soonest live bucket**. Magpie folds that into the window's pace, so the 50 points are spent first. Each window keeps its own `resetsAt`, so the card still shows each bucket's own expiry.
- When a bucket is spent and another live bucket remains, it is marked `aside` instead of staying as a `used: 100` window. This prevents burning the 50 from zeroing the account's pace and dropping it into the spent tier. If every bucket is spent, none is set aside, so an empty account still reads as used up.
- `tests/maas.test.mjs` covers both the 50/300 shape and the after-spend shape.
- `0.3.3` + CHANGELOG.

`npm test`: 342 passed, 0 failed.

issue.title: [feature] usage: Used or Left can count up to each account's usage cap (branch ready; PRs are collaborators-only)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Branch: [huangguang1999/magpie `usage-quota-up-to-cap`](https://github.com/huangguang1999/magpie/tree/usage-quota-up-to-cap), one commit, [7c17a3c](https://github.com/huangguang1999/magpie/commit/7c17a3cf961004d3cdc8e167cc8ab28cfa924fff), on origin/main f65fe92. I'm filing it as an issue because PRs here are limited to collaborators.

```
git fetch https://github.com/huangguang1999/magpie usage-quota-up-to-cap && git cherry-pick 7c17a3c
```

## What I want to do

I cap every Claude account at 95% (an account's usage cap). The Usage page's allowances then read the vendor's percentages, which say nothing of the cap. Across seven accounts the table read 16% of five hours used, as if most of it were there to use, while routing could use none of them: four had their week at the 95% cap, which holds their five hours, and one was past its cap in its five hours.

## What I do today instead

Open each account's row and work out by hand which ones a cap holds.

## The change

Subsystem: GUI app shell, the Usage page's allowances ([gui-shell.md](https://github.com/huangguang1999/magpie/blob/usage-quota-up-to-cap/docs/subsystems/gui-shell.md), updated in the commit).

- **Trigger:** the picked one of Used and Left in the Allowances head (`#quotaMode`) now says what its share is counted against. A click on it again opens a menu (`openProtoMenu`): **Whole allowance**, the vendor's percentage as before, or **Up to the cap**, each account's usage cap as 100%. The choice goes with either Used or Left and is kept on this computer (`magpie.quotaUnderCap`). The default is Whole allowance, so nothing changes until it is picked.
- **Before:** the shares are the vendor's, so 95% used of a 95% cap reads as 5% left, and five hours held by a week at its cap read as all left.
- **After (Up to the cap):** `capShares` in the usage plugin counts each share up to its cap, `min(100, used × 100 / cap)` (`windowCapOf`, a window's own cap by `WindowCapID`'s name). A window that another one at its cap stops the account past, `window_held.go`'s rule at the cap rather than at 100%, is all used and held by it (`heldBy`), so the all-accounts strip counts it as it counts the gateway's own holds. A week with room left behind five hours at their cap isn't held.
- **Where it applies:** `renderQuotas` passes the cards it draws through `capShares`, so the table, the cards, the all-accounts strip, the sort and the bars read the counted shares with no change of their own. `quotas` itself, the panel, the menu bar and routing are left as they were.
- **Limits:** `/api/usage/quotas` isn't sent through `WithCapped`, and a window's `Model` never reaches the GUI, so only a window named as a run of time alone ("5 hours", "Weekly") stops the whole account. One of some models ("7 days Opus"), a family's or a pool's is counted up to its cap and holds no other window. A card with no cap read yet, another magpie's, and windows of money, amounts or text are as the vendor says.
- **Budget:** the pick is drawn by `renderQuotaMode` in the usage plugin, like the trend pick beside it; app.js is 100 bytes smaller than main's. While its menu is open the pick isn't drawn again, as the page's refresh would otherwise leave the menu on a button no longer in the page.
- **Strings:** six new ones, each in zh, zh-TW, ja and de.

## Verification

Run at 7c17a3c (on origin/main f65fe92), go1.26.8 darwin/arm64:

- **A test that fails without it.** `usage-quota-cap.test.cjs` (new) passes 8/8. With `capShares` returning the cards as they are, 5 of 8 fail, e.g. "a share is counted up to the cap, the cap as 100%": actual `[47.5, 19]`, expected `[50, 20]`. The new test in `usage-quota-table.test.cjs` fails the same way: `.qt-group never said 73%: Claude Code 7 个账号 16% 83%`. With the pick drawn again while its menu is open, it fails with "the open menu's button is kept through a redraw". Restored, both pass.
- **GUI, chromium and webkit:** usage-quota-table 24/24, usage-all-accounts 24/24, usage-table-groups 40/40, usage-quota-head-gap 20/20, usage-remote-key-limits 20/20, panel-quota-lazy 20/20, builtins 4/4, idle-ticks 2/2. Without a browser: usage-merge 9/9, usage-stale-answer 11/11, i18n-keys 4/4, i18n-en-no-cjk 4/4, nav-timeout 1/1.
- **Vet and builds:** `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`, `go build`, `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui`, `GOOS=windows go build`: ok. No Go file changed.
- **`go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./...`** in a temporary HOME with Go's caches pinned: 96 packages ok; `TestCoreScriptBudget` passes, run alone at this commit. Red, each the same on origin/main f65fe92 run alone in a worktree of its own:
  - internal/gui: `TestBuiltinsTranslated` (#7257), `TestSettingsSaveKeepsWhatItDoesNotSend` (#7240), `TestLaneLimitRoutes` (#5150), `TestProxyCheckSaysAProxyPassedBy` (#2562)
  - build/darwin: `TestFreedHeapLeavesFootprint` (#6701)
  - internal/cli: `TestHealthcheckFindsTheRunningGatewayWithoutMagpieAddr`, `TestUpdateRestartsTheGatewayItFindsWithoutMagpieAddr`, `TestUpdateFindsAMagpieThatWroteNoRecord` (#6471)
  - internal/proc: `TestCombinedOutputOwnAnswersForItself` (#4795)
  - internal/provider `TestResolveVia`, and internal/gateway `TestClaudeAccountOffMovesToNextAccount`, `TestAutoModeClassifierOnTheClaudeBridge`, `TestClaudeRunSessionsAreTheBridges` and three `TestClaudeClientCache…`: no issue found, cause not looked into.
  - internal/agent and internal/library hit the 10m package timeout in the full run and weren't run again alone.
- **Real use:** this commit built and run as `magpie web` in a temporary HOME with copies of providers.json, logins.json, quotas.json and usage.jsonl, on its own port beside the running magpie, not touching it. Seven Claude accounts capped at 95%, five of them with their week at or past the cap:

  | | 5 hours | 7 days |
  |---|---|---|
  | Used, whole allowance (as before) | 0% | 79% |
  | Used, up to the cap | 71% | 83% |
  | Left, whole allowance (as before) | 100% | 21% |
  | Left, up to the cap | 29% | 17% |

  Each is what counting by hand from the same readings gives.

## Not tried

- Linux and Windows windows; only the GOOS vet and builds above were run.
- A provider with model, family or pool windows on a real account; those cases are covered by fixtures only.
- The panel and the menu bar, which this leaves as they were.

active.title: gateway/gui: cannot configure passHeaders or replyHeaders for plugin-backed providers in Web UI

new.body:
Thanks for the detailed root-cause and patch — it matches what I saw: on a plugin-backed account the Advanced header fields never render, and saving sends neither key, so I had to edit `providers.json` by hand.

The branch looks right. Could you open it as a PR against `yetone/magpie` so it can be reviewed and merged? The UI fix covers the reported case; the declarative `passHeaders` default from the second suggestion can stay a separate follow-up.

Happy to re-check the editor on my plugin-backed provider once a build with the fix is available.
